question: The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) for providing employment to people in drought prone areas was started by the Government of India during the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fourth Five-Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) was launched in 1973-74 during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74), to tackle drought conditions and generate employment in drought-prone areas. (सूखा प्रवण क्षेत्र कार्यक्रम — चतुर्थ पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• Its aim was optimum utilisation of land, water, livestock and human resources to increase agricultural productivity and provide employment.

 

• It was implemented on a watershed basis and jointly funded by the Centre and the states.

 

• DPAP was one of the earliest area-development programmes; it was later merged with related schemes under the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) in 2009.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPAP originally covered drought-prone parts of states like Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

 

• Similar area-development schemes include the Desert Development Programme (DDP), 1977-78.

 

NOTE

 

• Sixth Five-Year Plan (Option 2): Ran from 1980-85, well after DPAP had already started.

 

• Third Five-Year Plan (Option 3): Ran from 1961-66, before DPAP existed.

 

• Seventh Five-Year Plan (Option 4): Ran from 1985-90, long after DPAP was launched.

question: 'Padayani', a local dance form primarily performed in ________ to please Goddess Bhadrakali.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Padayani (also called Padeni) is a ritualistic art form performed in Bhadrakali temples of central Travancore, Kerala. (पडयनी नृत्य — केरल)

 

• It is mainly performed in temples of Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam and Idukki districts of Kerala.

 

• The performance features large, colourful face masks called 'kolam', made from arecanut sheaths and other natural materials, worn by dancers who perform to drum beats.

 

• It depicts the mythological battle between Goddess Kali and the demon Darika, and is performed to please Goddess Bhadrakali.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known dance/ritual art forms of Kerala include Theyyam, Mohiniyattam (a classical dance) and Kathakali.

 

• Padayani is usually performed during the temple festival season between January and May.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Known for dance forms like Bihu and Sattriya, not Padayani.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Known for Odissi and Chhau, not Padayani.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Known for Chhau (Purulia) and Kirtan traditions, not Padayani.

question:
Which of the following statements are true based on the 4NH3(g)+5O2(g)→4NO(g)+6H2O(g)?

(a) N gets oxidized.

(b) O gets oxidized.

(c) N gets reduced.

(d) O gets reduced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is (a) and (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the reaction 4NH3(g) + 5O2(g) → 4NO(g) + 6H2O(g), the oxidation state of nitrogen changes from -3 (in NH3) to +2 (in NO) — this is a rise in oxidation number, i.e. oxidation. (अमोनिया ऑक्सीकरण — नाइट्रोजन ऑक्सीकृत, ऑक्सीजन अपचयित)

 

• The oxidation state of oxygen changes from 0 (in O2) to -2 (in NO and H2O) — this is a fall in oxidation number, i.e. reduction.

 

• This reaction is a classic redox reaction and is also the first step of the industrial Ostwald process for manufacturing nitric acid.

 

• So statement (a) 'N gets oxidized' is true, and statement (d) 'O gets reduced' is true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Oxidation = increase in oxidation number / loss of electrons; reduction = decrease in oxidation number / gain of electrons.

 

• In this reaction, NH3 acts as the reducing agent and O2 acts as the oxidising agent.

 

NOTE

 

• (a) and (b) (Option 2): Statement (b) is wrong — oxygen is reduced, not oxidised, in this reaction.

 

• (c) and (d) (Option 3): Statement (c) is wrong — nitrogen is oxidised, not reduced, in this reaction.

 

• (b) and (c) (Option 4): Both statements are wrong for the reasons given above.

question: Which Indian musician from Maharashtra received the Padma Vibhushan 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain, the legendary tabla maestro from Mumbai, Maharashtra, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (India's second-highest civilian award) in 2023. (जाकिर हुसैन — पद्म विभूषण 2023)

 

• He was born in 1951 to tabla legend Ustad Alla Rakha, and became an internationally acclaimed percussionist and multiple Grammy Award winner.

 

• He was honoured under the Padma Awards 2023 list, announced around Republic Day, which also included figures like Raveena Tandon and M. M. Keeravani in other fields.

 

• Zakir Hussain passed away in December 2024 in San Francisco, USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zakir Hussain had earlier received the Padma Shri (1988) and the Padma Bhushan (2002), making him one of the few artists to receive all three Padma awards.

 

• He was celebrated for his collaborations across genres, including the fusion group Shakti with John McLaughlin.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramdas Palsule, Bharat Kamat and Milind Date (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these names correspond to the Padma Vibhushan 2023 awardee from Maharashtra referred to in this question; they are distractor options.

question: Which of the following is an example of major industrial region of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chota Nagpur region.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chota Nagpur Plateau region (spanning Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh) is one of the major industrial regions of India, based on rich mineral and power resources. (छोटा नागपुर औद्योगिक क्षेत्र — प्रमुख औद्योगिक क्षेत्र)

 

• It is a mineral-based heavy industrial belt, home to major steel plants at Jamshedpur, Bokaro, Durgapur and Rourkela.

 

• The region has rich deposits of coal, iron ore, mica and bauxite, which support its heavy and metallurgical industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major industrial regions of India include the Mumbai-Pune region, Hugli region, Bangalore-Tamil Nadu region, Gujarat region, Vishakhapatnam-Guntur region, Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut region and Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram region.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhojpur-Munger (Option 2), Jaipur-Ajmer (Option 3) and Bilaspur-Korba (Option 4): None of these is classified among India's major industrial regions in the standard geographical classification.

question: Raja Bhalindra Singh trophy is associated with which of the following national sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Games.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is awarded to the overall champion team (the team with the highest medal tally) at the National Games of India. (राजा भालिंद्र सिंह ट्रॉफी — राष्ट्रीय खेल)

 

• It is named after Raja Bhalindra Singh, a former President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and an IOC member.

 

• The Services (Services Sports Control Board) team has won this trophy multiple times in recent editions of the National Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India Games (Youth, University and Winter editions) are separate, age/category-specific multi-sport events distinct from the senior-level National Games.

 

• The National Games of India are organised periodically by the Indian Olympic Association in different host states.

 

NOTE

 

• Khelo India Youth Games (Option 1): An annual national-level multi-sport event for school-age athletes; does not award this trophy.

 

• Khelo India Winter Games (Option 2): The winter-sports edition of Khelo India, typically held in Jammu & Kashmir/Ladakh.

 

• Khelo India University Games (Option 3): The edition of Khelo India meant for university-level athletes.

question: The renowned ghazal singer Girija Devi was born in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Girija Devi, renowned Hindustani classical vocalist famed for Thumri, Chaiti and Kajri, was born in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh, in 1929. (गिरिजा देवी — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• She belonged to the Banaras (Seniya) gharana and was popularly known as the 'Thumri Queen' (Thumri ki Malika).

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1989) and the Padma Vibhushan (2016) for her contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Girija Devi passed away in October 2017 in Kolkata.

 

• Other prominent artists of the Banaras gharana include Ustad Bismillah Khan (shehnai) and Siddheshwari Devi (Thumri).

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1), Bihar (Option 2) and Punjab (Option 4): None of these is Girija Devi's birthplace; they are distractor states.

question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?
option_1: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
option_2: India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
option_3: All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
option_4: Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India follows a multi-party system, and political parties are classified by the Election Commission of India as National Parties, State (Regional) Parties, and registered-unrecognised parties. (भारत — बहुदलीय प्रणाली)

 

• The recognition and classification criteria for parties are laid down under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

 

• Party symbols are allotted by the Election Commission of India, not the President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The classification of parties as national or state parties is reviewed periodically by the Election Commission based on vote-share and seat criteria.

 

• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Party symbols are assigned by the Election Commission of India, not the President.

 

• Option 3: Parties are registered with the Election Commission of India, not the Supreme Court.

 

• Option 4: The status of a party (national/state) is accorded by the Election Commission, not by Parliament.

question: How was the growth in all food grains after the Green Revolution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Disproportionate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the Green Revolution, the growth in foodgrain production in India was disproportionate — the benefits were concentrated mainly in wheat and in a few states such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. (हरित क्रांति — असमान वृद्धि)

 

• The Green Revolution, starting from the mid-1960s, introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, irrigation and mechanisation, mainly benefiting wheat cultivation.

 

• Rice production also grew, but with a time lag and mostly in irrigated regions, while pulses and coarse cereals largely remained left behind.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India is closely associated with agricultural scientist M. S. Swaminathan, often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

 

• It made India largely self-sufficient in foodgrains but raised concerns about regional and crop-wise imbalance as well as environmental issues like soil degradation.

 

NOTE

 

• Unitary (Option 1), Proportionate (Option 2) and Unpredictable (Option 3): None of these correctly describes the skewed, uneven nature of foodgrain growth following the Green Revolution.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dual Citizenship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship for the entire country, unlike federations such as the USA that have dual citizenship (national and state). (भारतीय संविधान — एकल नागरिकता)

 

• Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship; India does not recognise dual citizenship (the OCI card is not equivalent to dual citizenship).

 

• India does have a Universal Adult Franchise (Article 326), an Independent Judiciary, and its amendment procedure under Article 368 makes it a 'blend of rigidity and flexibility'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card holders do not enjoy full citizenship rights such as voting or holding public office — it is a distinct status, not dual citizenship.

 

• The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Universal Adult Franchise (Option 1), Independent Judiciary (Option 2) and Blend of rigidity & flexibility (Option 4): All three are genuine, well-established features of the Indian Constitution.

question: The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended which of the following Acts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 (later enacted as an Act) amended the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, to add provisions against violence towards healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. (महामारी रोग अधिनियम, 1897 — संशोधन अध्यादेश 2020)

 

• The original Act of 1897 was enacted to tackle the outbreak of bubonic plague in Bombay and empowers governments to take special measures during epidemics.

 

• The 2020 amendment made acts of violence against healthcare personnel and damage to their property cognizable and non-bailable offences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, was invoked extensively by various state governments during the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

• It is one of the oldest public health laws still in use in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1892 (Option 1), 1895 (Option 2) and 1890 (Option 3): These are incorrect years; the Epidemic Diseases Act was actually enacted in 1897.

question: Under the 'Mero Rukh Mero Santati' initiative launched by the Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang in 2023, how many trees will be planted for every child born in Sikkim ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the 'Mero Rukh Mero Santati' ('My Tree, My Legacy') initiative launched by Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang in 2023, 100 trees are planted for every child born in the state. (मेरो रुख मेरो सन्तति — 100 पेड़)

 

• The scheme aims to promote afforestation and environmental conservation while linking tree plantation to the celebration of childbirth.

 

• It is implemented by the Sikkim Forest, Environment and Wildlife Management Department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state in 2016.

 

• Sikkim runs several other environment-linked initiatives that emphasise its green cover and promote eco-tourism.

 

NOTE

 

• 50 (Option 1), 150 (Option 2) and 200 (Option 4): These are incorrect figures; the scheme fixes the number at 100 trees per child born.

question: Filtration of waste products in humans happens in the kidneys. There is a large number of filtration units present inside the kidneys to help them in doing this job. These filtration units are called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is nephrons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nephrons are the structural and functional filtration units of the kidney; each human kidney contains about a million nephrons. (वृक्काणु/नेफ्रॉन — वृक्क की छानने की इकाई)

 

• Each nephron consists of a Bowman's capsule (enclosing a cluster of capillaries called the glomerulus) and a long renal tubule, which together carry out filtration, reabsorption and secretion.

 

• The Bowman's capsule is only the initial part of a nephron, not the complete filtration unit itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Blood is filtered under pressure in the glomerulus, and the resulting filtrate is refined into urine as it passes through the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule and collecting duct.

 

• Kidneys also help regulate blood pressure, electrolyte balance and pH of the body.

 

NOTE

 

• Bowman's capsules (Option 1): Only the cup-shaped initial part of a nephron, not the entire filtration unit.

 

• capillaries (Option 3): Tiny blood vessels forming the glomerulus inside the Bowman's capsule, not the filtration unit as a whole.

 

• alveoli (Option 4): Air sacs in the lungs involved in gas exchange, unrelated to kidney filtration.

question: Which number is called Avogadro's constant, named after the 19th century scientist Amedeo Avogadro?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.022 × 10^23.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Avogadro's constant (NA) is 6.022 × 10^23 per mole, representing the number of constituent particles (atoms, molecules or ions) present in one mole of a substance. (आवोगाद्रो संख्या — 6.022×10^23)

 

• It is named after the 19th-century Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro, who proposed that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules (Avogadro's Law).

 

• The value has been precisely fixed in the SI system since the 2019 redefinition of the mole.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of the mole and Avogadro's number is fundamental to stoichiometry in chemistry.

 

• Avogadro's number was first experimentally estimated by scientists such as Jean Perrin, and later named in Avogadro's honour.

 

NOTE

 

• 6.020 × 10^20 (Option 2), 6.032 × 10^19 (Option 3) and 6.012 × 10^21 (Option 4): All are incorrect values/orders of magnitude; the accepted value is 6.022 × 10^23.

question: Which branch of ecology deals with the characteristics of ancient environment and their relationship with ancient plants and animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paleoecology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Paleoecology is the branch of ecology that studies the characteristics of ancient (prehistoric) environments and their relationship with ancient plants and animals, often using fossil evidence. (पुरा पारिस्थितिकी — प्राचीन पर्यावरण अध्ययन)

 

• It combines ecology, geology and paleontology to reconstruct past ecosystems and understand environmental and evolutionary changes over geological time.

 

• It helps scientists understand extinct species and how ancient organisms interacted with their environments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related fields include palynology (study of pollen and spores) and paleobotany (study of ancient plants).

 

• Fossil records and sediment layers serve as key evidence sources in paleoecological studies.

 

NOTE

 

• Demecology (Option 1): The study of population ecology — the dynamics of populations of a single species.

 

• Ichthyology (Option 2): The branch of zoology dealing with the study of fish.

 

• Mycology (Option 4): The branch of biology dealing with the study of fungi.

question: Which of the following is a landlocked Salt Lake in South-West Asia between Israel and Jordan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dead Sea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dead Sea is a landlocked salt lake located between Israel and Jordan in South-West Asia, and is one of the saltiest water bodies in the world. (मृत सागर — इज़राइल-जॉर्डन के बीच)

 

• Its shoreline, about 430 m below sea level, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface.

 

• Its extremely high salinity (around 34%) makes it inhospitable for most aquatic life, giving it the name 'Dead Sea'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dead Sea is fed mainly by the Jordan River and has no outlet, so water concentrates through evaporation.

 

• It is famous for its therapeutic mud and for the high buoyancy that lets people float easily on its surface.

 

NOTE

 

• Don Juan Pond (Option 1): A hypersaline pond in Antarctica, the most saline water body in the world.

 

• Aral Sea (Option 2): A shrinking saline lake located between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

 

• Caspian Sea (Option 3): The world's largest inland body of water, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

question: Which of the following rivers is an east flowing river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Godavari river is an east-flowing river of Peninsular India, originating near Trimbakeshwar in Nashik, Maharashtra, and draining into the Bay of Bengal. (गोदावरी नदी — पूर्व की ओर बहने वाली नदी)

 

• It is the largest river of Peninsular India (after considering the Indus and Ganga at the national level) and is popularly called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South).

 

• Its main tributaries include the Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira and Wainganga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major east-flowing Peninsular rivers include the Mahanadi, Krishna, Kaveri and Penner, all of which drain into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• The Godavari basin covers parts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahi river (Option 1): A west-flowing river through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat, draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

 

• Narmada river (Option 2): A major west-flowing Peninsular river flowing through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.

 

• Tapi river (Option 4): Another west-flowing Peninsular river running roughly parallel to the Narmada, also draining into the Arabian Sea.

question: The Daroga system in 1792 was introduced by whom among the following Governor- Generals in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Cornwallis, Governor-General of India, introduced the Daroga system of policing in 1792 as part of his administrative and police reforms. (दरोगा प्रणाली — लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस, 1792)

 

• Under this system, each district was divided into thanas (police circles), each headed by a daroga (an Indian police officer), responsible for maintaining law and order.

 

• Cornwallis is also known for the Permanent Settlement of 1793 in Bengal and for laying the foundations of the Indian Civil Service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cornwallis served as Governor-General of India twice — from 1786 to 1793, and briefly again in 1805.

 

• He also introduced the separation of revenue collection and judicial functions in district administration.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Minto (Option 2): Known for the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909 and for granting separate electorates to Muslims.

 

• Lord Mayo (Option 3): Established the Statistical Survey of India and was assassinated in the Andaman Islands in 1872.

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 4): Known for social reforms, including the abolition of Sati (1829) and the introduction of English education (1835).

question: Chariot festival is dedicated to Lord Jagannath along with Subhadra and _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Balabhadra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival) of Puri, Odisha, is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, along with his elder brother Balabhadra (Balarama) and sister Subhadra. (रथ यात्रा — जगन्नाथ, बलभद्र और सुभद्रा)

 

• The three deities are taken out in a grand procession in three separate chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple.

 

• The festival is celebrated annually in the month of Ashadha (June-July) and is one of the most significant Hindu festivals of Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Jagannath's chariot is called 'Nandighosha', Balabhadra's is 'Taladhwaja', and Subhadra's is 'Darpadalana'.

 

• Rath Yatra festivals in the same tradition are also held elsewhere in India and around the world, notably at ISKCON temples.

 

NOTE

 

• Sudama (Option 2): A childhood friend of Lord Krishna, not part of the Jagannath trinity.

 

• Hanuman (Option 3): A devotee of Lord Rama, unrelated to the Jagannath Rath Yatra deities.

 

• Arjuna (Option 4): A Pandava prince from the Mahabharata, unrelated to the Jagannath trinity.

question: What correctly defines change of inventories of a firm during a year?
option_1: Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year
option_2: Production of the firm during the previous year – Sale of the firm during the year
option_3: Sale of the firm during the year – Production of the firm during the year
option_4: Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the previous year
solution_text:
The correct answer is Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The change in inventories (stock) of a firm during a year is calculated as Production during the year minus Sales during the year. (माल-सूची में परिवर्तन — उत्पादन घटा बिक्री)

 

• If production exceeds sales, inventories increase (positive change); if sales exceed production, inventories decrease (inventory decumulation).

 

• Inventory (unsold stock, raw materials, semi-finished goods) is treated as a form of investment expenditure in national income accounting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inventory investment is a component of Gross Domestic Capital Formation in the expenditure method of calculating national income.

 

• Both planned and unplanned changes in inventories count towards this calculation, regardless of whether the change was intended by the firm.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Incorrectly uses the previous year's production instead of the current year's, which is not the standard definition.

 

• Option 3: Reverses the correct formula (Sales − Production), which gives the negative of the actual change in inventories.

 

• Option 4: Incorrectly uses the previous year's sales instead of the current year's sales.

question: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?
option_3: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
option_4: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sports Authority of India (SAI), established in 1984, functions under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. (भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण — युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल मंत्रालय)

 

• SAI is the apex national sports body responsible for the promotion and development of sports infrastructure and the training of athletes across India.

 

• It administers schemes such as the National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC), SAI Training Centres (STC) and the Khelo India Scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports was created as an independent ministry in 2000, having earlier been part of the Ministry of Human Resource Development.

 

• The SAI headquarters is located in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Education (Option 1), Ministry of Social Justice (Option 2) and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Option 3): None of these administers the Sports Authority of India.

question: Which of the following kingdoms was divided into subdivisions called Aharas or Rashtras that meant districts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satavahana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satavahana kingdom (Deccan region, c. 1st century BCE to 3rd century CE) was divided into administrative subdivisions called Aharas or Rashtras, meaning districts. (सातवाहन साम्राज्य — आहार/राष्ट्र प्रशासनिक विभाजन)

 

• Each Ahara was governed by an official known as an Amatya; the Satavahanas had a well-organised administrative system, partly influenced by Mauryan patterns.

 

• The Satavahanas were notable patrons of Buddhism and are credited with early use of Prakrit in inscriptions such as those at Nashik and Naneghat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Notable Satavahana rulers include Simuka (founder) and Gautamiputra Satakarni, one of the most powerful rulers of the dynasty.

 

• The Satavahanas issued coins bearing portraits of rulers with legends in Prakrit, an important source for the numismatic history of the period.

 

NOTE

 

• Kushana (Option 1): A Central Asian dynasty ruling over northern India, known for Kanishka and the Gandhara/Mathura schools of art.

 

• Parthian (Option 2): Also called Pahlava, an Iranian dynasty with limited presence in north-western India.

 

• Shaka (Option 4): Central Asian rulers (Scythians) who established kingdoms in western and northern India, known for the Shaka era/Saka Samvat.

question: ______, authored by Tolkappiyar is the earliest Tamil literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tolkappiyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tolkappiyam, authored by Tolkappiyar, is considered the earliest extant work of Tamil literature and grammar. (तोल्काप्पियम — तमिल का प्राचीनतम ग्रंथ)

 

• It is a comprehensive treatise on Tamil grammar, poetics and rhetoric, and is regarded as the foundational text of the Sangam literary tradition.

 

• It is traditionally dated to around the 3rd century BCE, though its final compilation may be somewhat later.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangam literature is broadly classified into groups such as the Ettuthogai (Eight Anthologies) and Pathuppattu (Ten Idylls).

 

• Tolkappiyam is divided into three parts: Eluttadikaram (phonetics), Solladikaram (grammar) and Poruladikaram (subject matter/poetics).

 

NOTE

 

• Ettutogai (Option 2): A collection of eight anthologies of Sangam poetry; it is not the earliest work and was not authored solely by Tolkappiyar.

 

• Kalittogai (Option 3): One of the texts within the Ettuthogai anthology group of Sangam literature.

 

• Narrinai (Option 4): Another anthology within the Ettuthogai group, comprising Sangam-era poems.

question: Which Indian political leader was called as Lok Nayak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jai Prakash Narayan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jai Prakash Narayan (JP), a prominent freedom fighter and socialist leader, was popularly known as 'Lok Nayak' (People's Leader). (जय प्रकाश नारायण — लोकनायक)

 

• He led the 'Total Revolution' (Sampoorna Kranti) movement against the Indira Gandhi government in the mid-1970s, which eventually contributed to the imposition of the Emergency (1975-77).

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1999.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• JP was associated with the Congress Socialist Party before playing an active role in the Quit India Movement of 1942.

 

• In his later years he was also closely associated with Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan (land-gift) movement and the Sarvodaya movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Ram Manohar Lohia (Option 1): A noted socialist leader and thinker known for advocating non-Congressism; not called Lok Nayak.

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 3): Popularly known as 'Lokmanya' ('respected/accepted by the people'), not 'Lok Nayak'.

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose (Option 4): Popularly known as 'Netaji', the founder of the Indian National Army (INA).

question: Three Indians were featured in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people of 2021'. Whose name was NOT included in the list?
solution_text:

• Amitabh Bachchan was NOT among the three Indians featured in that particular 2021 list.

 

• The list recognises influential global figures across categories such as Icons, Titans, Leaders, Pioneers, Artists and Innovators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

• Narendra Modi and Mamata Banerjee were both featured in the 'Leaders' category of that year's list.

 

NOTE

 

• Narendra Modi (Option 1), Mamata Banerjee (Option 2) and Adar Poonawalla (Option 4): All three were indeed featured in TIME's 2021 list of the 100 most influential people.
